strengths: Clear and convincing toy model experiments with ground truth features demonstrating that L0 must be set precisely for SAEs to learn correct features
Important observation that reconstruction loss actually incentivizes low-L0 SAEs to learn incorrect features, undermining the sparsity-reconstruction tradeoff framing
Simple and robust Nth decoder projection metric that identifies optimal L0 in toy models and correlates with peak performance on sparse probing tasks
External validation via sparse probing benchmark showing predicted optimal L0 (200-250) matches observed peak F1 scores on Gemma-2-2b
Practical analysis of open-source SAEs revealing most use suboptimal L0 values, with clear implications for the field
Well-presented paper with clear figures, reproducible code, and effective narrative progression
Addresses a significant and underexamined practical problem in SAE training that practitioners currently treat as a free parameter
weaknesses: Severely limited LLM validation scope: tested on only one layer (layer 12) of one model (Gemma-2-2b) and one architecture (BatchTopK), making generalization to other models, layers, and SAE types completely unknown

Absence of ground truth in LLMs: no direct measurements of feature quality (monosemanticity, polysemanticity) on Gemma-2-2b; validation relies entirely on one downstream task (sparse probing) which may optimize for different objectives than interpretability
Incomplete theoretical justification for why Nth decoder projection metric should minimize at correct L0; the intuition is stated but not rigorously derived or ablated

Critical practical limitations for automatic L0 finding (Appendix A.4): requires extensive hyperparameter tuning, careful initialization, and prior knowledge of approximate correct L0; authors acknowledge strategy 'requires a lot of hyperparameter tuning to work in real LLMs'

Appendix A.3 reveals concerning local minima behavior: starting with low L0 and transitioning to correct L0 during training fails to recover correct features, limiting practical applicability of the findings
Architecture specificity: only BatchTopK is studied; generalization to L1 and JumpReLU SAEs (which use indirect L0 control) is unverified
Asymmetric treatment of the high L0 regime: degenerate solutions are described less rigorously than low L0 feature mixing, leaving questions about severity and nature of degradation
Task-specific validation: sparse probing is correlative validation; unclear if L0=200-250 remains optimal for other downstream interpretability goals or if this is specific to sparse probing
Missing sensitivity analyses and ablations: limited exploration of why N-based aggregation is principled, no comparison with alternative feature quality metrics
Insufficient analysis of why practitioners use low L0 in practice, limiting understanding of adoption barriers for recommendations

strengths: Well-designed toy model experiments with clear ground truth demonstration of feature mixing under incorrect L0
Important empirical observation that reconstruction loss incentivizes incorrect feature mixing (contradicting sparsity-reconstruction tradeoff narrative)
Clear presentation with accessible explanations and effective visualizations (especially Figure 1)
Sparse probing validation provides some external support for the proposed metric
Honest discussion of limitations in Appendix A.6
weaknesses: Severely limited LLM validation: only one layer (layer 12) of one model (Gemma-2-2b) with no cross-layer or cross-model ablations, making generalizability claims unsupported
The concept of a single 'true L0' is questionable for real LLMs where features may be inherently polysemantic and not discretely separable like in toy models

Circular validation logic: s^dec_n metric is derived from feature observations, then sparse probing (which depends on feature quality) is used to validate it; these are not independent checks, and sparse probing may not be the right target metric
Proposed automatic L0-finding method (Appendix A.4) admittedly 'requires a lot of hyperparameter tuning' and doesn't work well on real LLMs, undermining practical utility
No analysis of the substantial computational cost: optimal L0=200-250 is 2-4x higher than typical L0, implying 2-4x larger encoder/decoder matrices, but trade-offs are not discussed
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple seeds reported for sparse probing results
Ad-hoc metric design: s^dec_n lacks theoretical justification; choice of N is heuristic ('h/2 seems to work'); alternative metrics not explored
Incomplete analysis of high L0 regime: paper shows 'degenerate solutions' but provides no mechanistic explanation for why
Alternative explanations not considered: could improved sparse probing at high L0 reflect greater representational capacity rather than correct features?
Overstated claims: statements about what 'our work shows' are based on single-layer evidence; strong generalization claims not justified by limited scope
Only BatchTopK SAEs tested despite claims findings should generalize to L1 and JumpReLU; this is stated as expectation with no supporting evidence

strengths: Important practical contribution challenging the assumption that L0 is a free parameter; directly impacts how practitioners should train SAEs
Well-designed toy model experiments with ground truth clearly demonstrate the phenomenon and reveal mechanisms like feature hedging and asymmetric effects of too-low vs. too-high L0
Simple, practical Nth decoder projection metric that is easy to compute without ground truth and works consistently across different parameter values
Meaningful LLM validation through correlation with sparse probing performance; agreement between s^dec_n minimum (200-250) and sparse probing peak is convincing
Excellent presentation with clear figures and thorough documentation; code and experimental details support reproducibility
Demonstrates real-world implications by showing existing SAEs on Neuronpedia use suboptimal L0 values
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations without defensive posturing
weaknesses: Severely limited LLM scope: only Gemma-2-2b layer 12 investigated thoroughly; generalization to other models, layers, and architectures is assumed but untested, limiting confidence in universal claims about 'most SAEs'

Theoretical justification for the Nth decoder projection metric is intuitive but not rigorous; why minimizing this metric specifically captures feature correctness is assumed rather than formally established
Validation through sparse probing is indirect; lacks direct evaluation of feature interpretability, monosemanticity, or performance on other downstream tasks beyond sparse probing

Automatic L0 detection (Section A.4) is underdeveloped and requires substantial hyperparameter tuning; authors acknowledge it 'requires a lot of hyperparameter tuning to work in real LLMs,' limiting practical applicability
No systematic investigation of how optimal L0 varies across layers, model sizes, and datasets despite claiming this is an important dependency; provides limited guidance for practitioners
Limited feature quality assessment beyond sparse probing; no direct human evaluation of interpretability or evaluation on tasks beyond sparse probing
Mechanism of feature hedging in LLMs is assumed rather than demonstrated; toy model results don't rigorously establish that the same mechanism causes the observations in real LLMs
Missing analysis of why too-high L0 produces degenerate mixtures while still learning many correct latents, whereas too-low L0 affects every latent; this asymmetry deserves deeper investigation
Practical guidance is limited for practitioners who cannot afford to train many SAEs at different L0 values to find the optimum
Empirical claims about 'most commonly used SAEs' being suboptimal rest on a single layer of one model, which overstates the generality of findings

strengths: Clear identification and demonstration of a critical problem: when L0 is incorrectly set, SAEs fail to disentangle features and mix correlated features instead. The paper convincingly shows that ground-truth correct features achieve worse reconstruction than those mixing features (Section 3.4), challenging conventional sparsity-reconstruction tradeoff thinking.

Excellent toy model experiments with clear progression from simple to complex scenarios, explicit control of ground-truth features, systematic variation of correlation structures, and convincing visualization of the mechanism. This methodologically strong validation clearly demonstrates the core phenomenon.

Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple dimensions: two SAE architectures (BatchTopK, JumpReLU), multiple LLM layers, and connection to downstream sparse probing performance. The practical finding that most public SAEs have suboptimal L0 < 100 is valuable.

Novel practical contribution: the nth decoder projection metric (s^dec_n) provides a model-agnostic approach to detect L0 misspecification without requiring ground-truth features, demonstrating clear minima in toy models and interpretable behavior in LLM experiments.

Honest treatment of limitations, transparent discussion of when methods work and don't work (e.g., A.6 automatic optimization fails in practice), and generally good reproducibility documentation with promised code release.
weaknesses: Limited scope of LLM validation: only 2 LLM architectures tested (Gemma-2-2b, Llama-3.2-1b) with only 2-3 layers per model. Computational constraints are acknowledged but this significantly limits the generalizability of claims about what L0 'should be' for LLMs.

The proposed metric has significant practical limitations: still requires expensive L0 sweep during evaluation (not solved during training), shows noisier behavior in LLMs than toy models (e.g., Gemma layer 5 has no clear global minimum, only an 'elbow'), sensitivity to hyperparameter n, and inconsistent results with alternative metrics (Figure 15). The attempted automatic optimization (A.6) fails in practice and requires extensive hyperparameter tuning.

Circular validation through sparse probing: the paper validates optimal L0 against sparse probing performance, but sparse probing is itself just another evaluation metric, not ground-truth feature quality. No human evaluation of whether higher L0 actually produces more interpretable features, leaving causal claims partially unsupported.

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: while the paper empirically shows that MSE incentivizes feature mixing, it lacks theoretical explanation of why SAEs choose mixing over learning feature subsets, provides no analysis of optimization landscape, and doesn't examine information-theoretic trade-offs. The mechanism behind feature hedging at low L0 remains somewhat opaque.

The definition of 'correct L0' is not sufficiently examined: the paper conflates the data's intrinsic sparsity with optimal L0 for interpretability and downstream tasks. No consideration of whether real LLM features satisfy the linear representation hypothesis, no discussion of beneficial trade-offs from accepting some feature mixing, and no formal definition of 'monosemantic.'

JumpReLU's superior robustness to high L0 (per-latent threshold adjustment, Figure A.10) suggests the problem is architecture-dependent rather than universal, potentially undermining the universality of the 'correct L0' finding. This important limitation deserves more prominent discussion.

Incomplete code reference: 'Code is available at' appears without actual URL, harming reproducibility verification. Also missing ablation studies on SAE loss functions, decoder initialization, and LRH sensitivity.

Validation methodology has some circularity: the connection to downstream sparse probing performance is an empirical observation rather than causal evidence. The paper doesn't establish whether optimization toward the proposed metric actually leads to more interpretable features through human evaluation.

strengths: Clear empirical demonstration using well-designed toy models with ground-truth features showing that SAEs mix correlated features at incorrect L0 values
Valuable critique of sparsity-reconstruction tradeoff plots, showing that ground-truth SAEs can achieve worse reconstruction than incorrect SAEs at low L0
Validation on real LLMs (Gemma-2-2b, Llama-3.2-1b) showing alignment between metric and sparse probing performance
Well-written paper with effective visualizations that clearly illustrate the main phenomena
Practical observation that most open-source SAEs have L0 values that may be sub-optimal
Honest discussion of limitations in Appendix A.8
weaknesses: Limited novelty relative to concurrent work: Core insights about feature hedging due to insufficient sparsity are substantially discussed in Chanin et al. (2025); present work feels incremental

Weak theoretical justification for s^dec_n metric: The connection between near-zero decoder projections and monosemanticity lacks rigorous grounding; choice of n≈h/2 is heuristic and varies across SAE types

Impractical proposed solution: Finding correct L0 requires training multiple SAEs at different L0 values (computationally expensive); automatic approach acknowledged as requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning and having limited utility

Limited validation: Relies primarily on sparse probing as ground truth (itself limited); only 2 LLM models and few layers tested; no empirical demonstration of actual sparse probing improvements when using the proposed L0
Incomplete analysis: L0-too-high regime under-explored despite being mentioned; interesting observation in Section 4.2 about simultaneous too-high/too-low latents is mentioned but not developed
Conceptual ambiguities: 'Correct L0' operationally defined by where s^dec_n is minimized, but this may not equal ground-truth monosemantic L0; conflates different notions of correctness

Missing key experiments: No comparison of sparse probing F1 at different L0 values including the 'correct' L0; no analysis of computational cost-benefit; no comparison with alternative solutions (e.g., larger decoders, modified training objectives)
Overclaimed significance of Neuronpedia analysis (Figure 16): Limited data, doesn't account for different datasets/objectives, may reflect community choices rather than true sub-optimality
Theoretical understanding limited: Paper shows the phenomenon but lacks mechanistic explanation for why MSE loss incentivizes feature mixing (only one MSE comparison in Section 3.3)
Metric requires arbitrary hyperparameter choices and shows inconsistent behavior at high L0 across different n values (Figures 17-19)

strengths: Excellent experimental progression from controlled toy models with ground-truth features to real LLM validation, making the core phenomenon convincing and accessible

Rigorous toy model experiments using ground-truth SAE baselines that powerfully demonstrate how low-L0 SAEs achieve better reconstruction than correct SAEs, effectively critiquing standard evaluation practices

Valuable practical contribution: identifies that widely-used sparsity-reconstruction tradeoff plots can be misleading and proposes diagnostic metrics (nth decoder projection, decoder pairwise cosine similarity) to find correct L0
Real-world validation showing the proposed metric corresponds to peak sparse probing performance across different LLM architectures (Gemma, Llama) and SAE types (BatchTopK, JumpReLU)
Comprehensive experimental scope with thorough appendix covering alternative metrics, architecture comparisons, attempted automatic L0 finding, and honest limitations discussion
Clear, well-written presentation with effective visualizations (especially Figure 1) that make complex concepts accessible
Reproducibility: code promised, detailed experimental procedures, sufficient documentation for reproduction
weaknesses: Limited novelty of core mechanism: feature hedging was identified by Chanin et al. (2025); this work's main contribution is applying it to L0 selection and proposing diagnostic metrics, which is somewhat incremental

Proposed metrics lack strong theoretical justification: s_dec_n is intuitive but ad-hoc; choice of n requires empirical tuning with no principled justification; plateaus at high L0 making it difficult to detect when L0 is too high; alternative metric performs comparably but authors don't clearly justify preference

Automatic L0 finding unsuccessful (A.6): requires extensive hyperparameter tuning and is deemed 'complex and limited in utility' by authors themselves, severely limiting practical applicability—practitioners still need expensive sweeps

Incomplete characterization of high-L0 regime: claims of 'degenerate solutions' lack depth; Section 4.2 reveals some latents may be simultaneously too high and too low, undermining the central claim that a single correct L0 exists
Limited scope of LLM experiments: only 2 models tested, few specific layers, no investigation of layer-to-layer variation, and only 3 seeds per L0 creating visible variance in results

Gap between toy model assumptions and real LLMs: assumes perfectly orthogonal features and clean patterns; real features may be non-linear or non-orthogonal; robustness under violations of LRH unexplored

Inadequately defined 'correct L0': unclear if it's simply the mean number of active features; doesn't address what happens when underlying features aren't truly monosemantic; Section 4.2 suggests L0 may be latent-dependent

Limited characterization of practical impact: sparse probing improvements are modest (F1 ~0.80-0.82); unclear which downstream tasks benefit most; no guidance on whether practitioners should prioritize this over other SAE improvements

Practical solution incomplete: requires computationally expensive sweeps with no guidance on range/granularity; flat region in metric makes pinpointing optimum difficult; no actionable guidance for practitioners with limited resources
Sparsity-reconstruction critique underspecified: correctly identifies plots as misleading but proposes no alternative practical evaluation framework for practitioners without ground-truth SAEs
